title: Testing an acoustic model of the P-center in English and Japanese
why_promising: JASA production study with manually annotated English vowel onsets/syllable boundaries and Japanese annotations completed by a native phonetician then checked/corrected by the first author; OSF project provides example annotations and sound materials.
open_question: Verify whether OSF contains the complete token-level primary recordings/annotations or only examples and derived synchronization data; admit only if the full manually annotated production dataset is publicly downloadable.

title: Dimensionality Reduction in Lingual Articulation of Vowels: Evidence From Lax Vowels in Northern Anglo-English
why_promising: Primary laboratory ultrasound/acoustic vowel corpus: 40 Northern English speakers, 1,927 recorded lax-vowel tokens (1,857 analyzed); MFA vowel boundaries were subsequently checked and manually corrected as required.
open_question: Locate an openly downloadable repository containing the primary acoustic/ultrasound observations or corrected TextGrids. The open article verifies manual correction but does not surface a public data deposit in the current crawl.

title: A multimodal speech-production dataset with time-aligned articulography, EEG, audio, and vocal-tract anatomy
why_promising: Very large newly collected multimodal production resource: 29 German speakers, about 17 h EMA plus matched audio, EEG, anatomical measurements, public CC-BY-4.0 SWISSUbase release.
open_question: The dataset is richly instrumented but the published event/articulatory onsets are algorithmically detected from EMA velocities/TTLs. Verify whether any speech-segment or articulatory landmarks were manually annotated or exhaustively human-verified before admission under the strict manual-grounding rule.

title: mngu0 multimodal articulatory corpus — manually segmented acoustic prompt layer
why_promising: Primary British-English multimodal articulatory corpus; JASA documentation states high-quality acoustic recordings were manually segmented into prompts and corresponding segmentation data are distributed with the corpus.
open_question: Determine whether the released phone_labels/other fine-grained tiers were themselves manually created or corrected. Prompt-level segmentation alone may be too coarse for the core phonetic-token database; also document current registration terms/license before inclusion.
